facts.raw_span: a 4-year history of a slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion
a 1 cm × 0.5 cm macule, which progressively increased in size without symptoms
brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion
multiple pigmented papules of various sizes involved the vermilion of the upper left lip
brownish skin discoloration extending from 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth to the left philtral ridge
the lip was slightly swollen
a 1.5 cm lesion extended from the labial frenum to 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth
it was non-tender, non-indurated, and exhibited focal ulcerations
no cervical lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions were found
Results of a complete blood count, biochemical profile, and urinalysis were within normal limits
chest radiography was unremarkable
a computed tomography scan of the head and neck was performed to assess local extent of the lesion and to evaluate regional lymph nodes

concepts.why: The patient's slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion, with multiple pigmented papules and brownish skin discoloration, is consistent with labial melanoma, which can present with similar clinical features.

The patient's brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion and the presence of multiple pigmented papules are consistent with labial lentigo maligna, a type of skin cancer that can present with similar clinical features.

The patient's multiple pigmented papules on the lip, although not diagnostic on their own, could be part of the broader clinical picture of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, which includes mucocutaneous melanin deposits and can present with similar oral lesions.

aliases: Melanotic macule of the oral mucosa
concepts.why: The patient's initial presentation with a macule that progressively increased in size could be consistent with an oral melanotic macule, a benign pigmented lesion of the oral mucosa.

The patient's lesion with focal ulcerations could be suggestive of Kaposi's sarcoma, especially given the lesion's size and location, although other clinical features and diagnostic tests would be necessary to confirm this diagnosis.
